title: A regular map factoring through a localization is regular from the localization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $W\subset A$ a multiplicative subset with localization map $\lambda:A\to W^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\psi:W^{-1}A\to C$ a ring map. If the composite $\psi\circ\lambda:A\to C$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $\psi$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07PT (more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring-maximal-ideals, line 12392), sentence 'Since it factors through the localization R_p, also the ring map R_p -> (R_m^)_{p'}^ is regular', stated without proof; flatness: algebra.tex Lemma Tag 00HT (2) (lemma-flat-localization); primes of W^{-1}A: algebra.tex Lemma Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization)

proof.text: Write $A'=W^{-1}A$ and $\varphi=\psi\circ\lambda$. The $A$-module structure of $C$ given by $\varphi$ is the restriction along $\lambda$ of its $A'$-module structure given by $\psi$. Since $\varphi$ is regular, it is flat [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], i.e. $C$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] (with $M=C$; $\lambda$ satisfies (a)-(c) of that node by the definition of $W^{-1}A$), $C$ is a flat $A'$-module, i.e. $\psi$ is flat.

Fix a prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$, put $\mathfrak q=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$ and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak q')=A'_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak q'A'_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], an $A'$-algebra and, via $\lambda$, an $A$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $\mathfrak q$ is a prime ideal of $A$ with $\mathfrak q\cap W=\emptyset$, and $\lambda$ induces an isomorphism of fields and of $A$-algebras $\sigma:\kappa(\mathfrak q)=A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}k$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00E3 (algebra-lemma-spec-localization, line 3163) and basic notion Tag 00C9 (algebra-item-localization-localization, line 223)

proof.text: The ring map $\ell:C\otimes_Ak\to C\otimes_{A'}k$, $c\otimes x\mapsto c\otimes x$, is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras ($k$ acting on the right factor). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with $R=A$, $S=W$, the localization $\lambda:A\to A'$, $M=M'=C$, $N=N'=k$ and $\ell_M=\mathrm{id}_C$, $\ell_N=\mathrm{id}_k$. These identities are localizations at $W$: (a) $w\in W$ acts on $C$ as multiplication by $\psi(\lambda(w))$ and on $k$ as multiplication by the image of $\lambda(w)$, both invertible because $\lambda(w)$ is a unit of $A'$; (b) and (c) hold with $s=1$. Hence $\ell$, which is $m\otimes n\mapsto\ell_M(m)\otimes\ell_N(n)$, is a localization of $C\otimes_Ak$ at $W$. Every $w\in W$ acts bijectively on $C\otimes_Ak$: it acts as $\mu_w\otimes\mathrm{id}$, $\mu_w$ the multiplication by $\psi(\lambda(w))$ on $C$, whose inverse is $\mu_w^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}$ ($\mu_w^{-1}$, multiplication by $\psi(\lambda(w)^{-1})$, is $A$-linear). So by (c), $\ell(t)=0$ gives $wt=0$ for some $w$, hence $t=0$; and by (b) every element of $C\otimes_{A'}k$ is $w^{-1}\ell(t)=\ell(w^{-1}t)$. Thus $\ell$ is bijective; it is multiplicative and unital on pure tensors, hence a ring isomorphism, and $\ell(1\otimes x)=1\otimes x$, so it is $k$-linear.

proof.text: Let $F=C\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, the fibre ring of $\varphi$ at $\mathfrak q$, and $F'=C\otimes_{A'}k$, the fibre ring of $\psi$ at $\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $\sigma$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras (Step 2), $\mathrm{id}_C\otimes\sigma:F\to C\otimes_Ak$ is a ring isomorphism with inverse $\mathrm{id}_C\otimes\sigma^{-1}$. Composing with $\ell$ of Step 3 gives a ring isomorphism $\Theta:F\to F'$, $c\otimes x\mapsto c\otimes\sigma(x)$; in particular $\Theta(x f)=\sigma(x)\Theta(f)$ for $x\in\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $f\in F$.

source.place: Definition Tag 07BZ (more-algebra-definition-regular): the fibre rings; functoriality of the tensor product, written out by the agent

proof.text: $F'$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Since $\varphi$ is regular, $F$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; $F'\cong F$ as rings (Step 4), so $F'$ is Noetherian. Let $k'/k$ be a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] and regard $k'$ as an extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ via $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\xrightarrow{\sigma}k\subseteq k'$. As $\sigma$ is a field isomorphism, $k'/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is again finite purely inseparable (the same degree; every element of $k'$ has a $p$-th power iterate in $k=\sigma(\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, resp. $k'=k$ in characteristic $0$). The maps $k'\times F\to k'\otimes_kF'$, $(y,f)\mapsto y\otimes\Theta(f)$, and $k'\times F'\to k'\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}F$, $(y,f')\mapsto y\otimes\Theta^{-1}(f')$, are balanced over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ resp. $k$ because $\Theta(xf)=\sigma(x)\Theta(f)$, and induce mutually inverse ring isomorphisms $k'\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}F\cong k'\otimes_kF'$. The left side is a regular ring by the geometric regularity of $F$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, and regularity [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian with regular local rings at all primes) is invariant under ring isomorphisms, so $k'\otimes_kF'$ is regular.

proof.text: By Step 1 $\psi$ is flat, and by Steps 2-5 the fibre ring $C\otimes_{A'}\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ for every prime $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$; so $\psi$ is a regular ring map by definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].
